biography: Ricardo Fragnani was born in the heart of São Paulo, Brazil, amidst the constant roar of engines from a nearby karting track. Unlike most aspiring racers, Ricardo's family had no motorsport pedigree. His father was a mechanic, and Ricardo spent countless hours in the garage, learning the intricate dance of gears and pistons. At age 12, he built his first kart from spare parts, and promptly won his first amateur race. This victory cemented his passion. Formula Dirt took notice after a stunning performance in the Brazilian regional championship, where he drove a severely underpowered kart to a podium finish in every race. Now, at 24, Fragnani is considered one of Formula Dirt’s rising stars, known for his clinical precision and unwavering focus. He is quietly but determinedly working his way up the ranks.
drivingStyle: Fragnani's driving style is best described as calculating and precise. He is not one for flamboyant overtakes or daring maneuvers. Instead, he prefers to meticulously analyze the track, identify optimal braking points, and conserve tire wear. He excels in long races where strategy and consistency are paramount. While some may see him as cautious, his ability to maintain consistent lap times under immense pressure has proven to be a formidable weapon.

rivalries.reason: Bellini, a flamboyant Italian driver, constantly clashes with Fragnani's reserved style, often dismissing him as 'too boring' for the sport. Their differing approaches to racing and personalities frequently lead to on-track battles and heated exchanges off the track.

Volkov and Fragnani have a strategic rivalry. Both are incredibly calculating, and each sees the other as the biggest threat to their championship aspirations. Their battles are often chess matches on wheels, with each trying to outsmart the other.

quirks: Always polishes his helmet visor with a microfiber cloth exactly seven times before each race.
Insists on drinking the same brand and flavor of Brazilian Guarana soda before every qualifying session.
Carries a small, worn-out wrench in his pocket as a good luck charm, a relic from his karting days.
famousQuote: "Victory isn't about being the fastest for a single lap. It's about being the smartest for every lap."
careerHighlight: Winning the Interlagos Grand Prix in his rookie year. He started 12th on the grid and patiently picked off his rivals, capitalizing on their mistakes and conserving his tires to take the lead in the final laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the Monaco Grand Prix due to a rare misjudgment. The incident cost him valuable championship points and damaged his reputation for consistency.
